## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Repeatedly remove all vertices of an induced P4. This produces a cograph modulator X with |X| ≤ 4k in polynomial time.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_q(k)$ |
| Clauses | $k^{O(qg(q))}$ |
| Maximum clause width | $\max\{q,2,qg(q)\}$ |

## Derivation

1. Use one-hot color variables only on X, including properness and list constraints inside X.

2. The cited theorem gives a NO-subinstance on at most g(q) outside vertices whenever an assignment to X cannot be extended. Each removed color on such a vertex has a witness neighbor in X. Thus at most qg(q) color assignments on X suffice to witness nonextension.

3. Enumerate partial color assignments on at most qg(q) vertices of X. If such an assignment makes List Coloring on G-X impossible, forbid it by one clause. The required outside test is polynomial-time for fixed q on cographs.

4. Every nonextendible full assignment is forbidden and every extendible one survives. The width is fixed and the variable count is O_q(k), so the general-density bound applies.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- q is fixed; the constants and polynomial degree may be very large.
- This is a decision reduction and does not preserve coloring multiplicities.
- Cluster-deletion distance is a special case because every cluster graph is a cograph.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
